refresh_policy.notes: Atmospheric greenhouse concentrations and forcing summaries should refresh on a 6-8 week cadence unless a specific scientific release justifies an earlier update.

signals.label: Atmospheric CO2 concentration
signals.notes: Useful as the primary long-lived carbon forcing proxy for the carbon-emission anchor.

signals.label: Atmospheric CH4 concentration
signals.notes: Useful as the primary methane forcing proxy for the methane anchor.

temperature_inference.recommended_use: Use CO2 and CH4 as long-lived forcing inputs, not as a standalone temperature model.
why_not: Observed global temperature also depends on nitrous oxide and other long-lived greenhouse gases.
Short-lived aerosols, clouds, and albedo changes materially affect realized warming.
Ocean heat uptake and internal variability change how forcing translates into observed annual temperature.
Surface-temperature feedbacks are not captured by concentration-only proxies.
temperature_inference.platform_guidance: Keep the global temperature anchor calibrated to observed temperature anomaly products and use CO2 and CH4 to explain forcing pressure behind that outcome.
